L-glessner-rainwater-2221
      Rainwater fitting stock and concealed connections
      
    
    
    Decision
    The early Taylor 2135 photograph locates the framed Prairie Avenue heads and broad leader straps. Unrestricted HABS01 and HABS14 distinguish the small service collector from the north tower's ribbed bowl. Those later views corroborate geometry, not the survival of each fitting unchanged from 1904. Licensed modern w_lemay courtyard photographs (159537087 and 159537053, CC BY-SA 2.0) bound the rectangular court leaders and box troughs; their bright-green patina and modern round inspection caps are not carried into 1904. The copied HABS05 publication photograph remains rights-uncleared and supplies no new derived fitting geometry. The 180 by 140 mm gutters, 3 mm sheet stock, ordinary 105 mm rectangular leaders, 75 mm upper tower pipe, collar thickness, wall-return tabs, under-eave supports and concealed offsets are reconstructed. The dining and bow court leaders alone use 160 by 100 mm stock with shallow 2.5 mm front fluting and 400 mm strap spans, bounded by the modern 159537087 photograph rather than a measured 1904 specification. Full uses seven flutes and Light three. Prairie straps span 300 mm and sit at reconstructed heights 1.74, 4.07 and 6.30 m: their centres follow Taylor in the fixed wall-control camera fit, not an independent survey. Head width/height bounds are 370/590 mm for the Prairie panel, 490/880 mm for the north bowl, and 230/300 mm for the plain service collector. The early scan does not resolve a cast emblem: the framed relief and central boss are explicitly bounded stock ornament. Frame relief is 14 mm, bead diameter 24 mm, and the plain boss is 38 percent of head width; no legible emblem is invented. The north bowl's four flared ribs are similarly an interpretation, not a measured casting. The 104-degree tower outlet azimuth follows the HABS14 camera reading; absolute eave/grade and camera disagreements remain recorded for T-2228. Every collector follows the retained roof edge and has an outlet to a receiver, leader or descending branch. The north tower feeds its bowl rather than ending over the roof. The two east-court eave fragments receive reconstructed leaders beside the stair drum, clear of all axial openings. The north-court return connects below the bow eave without an uphill pipe or a sheet crossing windows. Street leaders enter grade; court/alley shoes are modest bounded discharges, not a claim about hidden underground drains. Supports enter existing masonry and roof-edge stock. A separate matte grey-green oxidised/coated finish (linear RGB 0.085/0.095/0.090, roughness 0.72, metallic fraction 0.15) is reconstructed for 1904, not colour or an identified alloy recovered from monochrome photographs. The shared near-black iron made the head relief unreadable in the first web close-up; the separate finish keeps other ironwork unchanged and costs one additional material primitive per tier. Light keeps the paths, heads, straps and apertures, simplifying only small rolled lips and curved sampling.

    T-2221.
